# Executive Summary

This laboratory investigates the relationship between vehicle
weight and fuel efficiency using the mtcars dataset.

R and Python independently estimated the same linear regression
model. Their previously observed results agreed within a
numerical tolerance of 0.0001.

# Research Question

How is vehicle weight associated with miles per gallon?

# Dataset

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

dataset <- read.csv("mtcars.csv")

stopifnot(
  nrow(dataset) == 32,
  all(c("mpg", "wt") %in% names(dataset))
)

head(dataset)
```

# Statistical Analysis

The model is:

$$
MPG_i = \beta_0 + \beta_1 Weight_i + \epsilon_i
$$

```{r}
model <- lm(mpg ~ wt, data = dataset)
summary(model)

print(coef(summary(model)))
```

# Visualization

```{r}
ggplot(dataset, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point(color = "steelblue", size = 3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE) +
  labs(
    title = "Vehicle Weight and Fuel Efficiency",
    x = "Weight (1,000 lbs)",
    y = "Miles per Gallon"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```


## Cross-Language Validation

R and Python independently estimated the same ordinary
least squares regression model using the same 32 observations.

The R reference values were exported at full numerical
precision to `r_reference.csv`.

The Python implementation independently calculated the
intercept, slope, and R-squared. The earlier full-precision
comparison passed for all three metrics.

```{r}
# Load the full-precision R reference
reference <- read.csv("r_reference.csv")

# Confirm the expected metrics exist
stopifnot(
  identical(
    reference$metric,
    c("intercept", "slope", "r_squared")
  ),
  all(is.finite(reference$value))
)

# Display the full-precision R results
print(reference, digits = 17)
```

The independently executed Python validation reported:

- Intercept difference: approximately 2.13e-14
- Slope difference: approximately 8.88e-16
- R-squared difference: approximately 1.11e-16

All three comparisons passed.

These results demonstrate numerical agreement between
the independently implemented R and Python regression
calculations.

The Python comparison was completed separately and
is not rerun during this Quarto render.


### Automated Regression Testing

The Python regression implementation was evaluated
using pytest within the project's dedicated virtual
environment.

The automated test suite contains seven tests:

1. Dataset observation count
2. Required R reference metrics
3. Intercept agreement
4. Weight coefficient agreement
5. R-squared agreement
6. Negative weight coefficient
7. Valid R-squared range

The cross-language comparisons use an absolute
numerical tolerance of 1e-10.

#### Recorded Test Results

- Test framework: pytest 9.2.0
- Python numerical library: NumPy 2.2.6
- Tests executed: 7
- Tests passed: 7
- Tests failed: 0
- Execution time: 0.03 seconds

All seven tests passed during the previously
completed laboratory execution.

These results represent a recorded test execution.
The pytest suite is not automatically rerun when
this Quarto document is rendered.

#### Reproduction Command

From the Positron-Lab-01 project directory:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_regression.py -v
```

The Python dependencies are recorded in
`requirements.txt`.



# Interpretation

The regression indicates a negative association between
vehicle weight and fuel efficiency.

The model explains approximately 75.28% of the observed
variation in miles per gallon.

This observational relationship does not establish causality.
